title: Clean-Out Between Stages
short_answer: Clean-out is how the next trade starts without eating our dust — flip Cleaned Out on Job Check only when it’s true.
summary: What "clean" means after hang, scrape, sand, ACT, and paint — and when Cleaned Out on Job Check is honest.
plain_words: Clean-out is not a courtesy to the GC. It is how the next trade (or our own finisher) starts without eating our dust and scrap. Marking Cleaned Out while screw points and mud buckets are still on the floor teaches Monday a lie.
when_to_use: After hang, scrape, sand, ACT, or stage completion
Before inviting the next trade into the room
prerequisites: Stage work actually complete enough to clear the floor

steps.body: After hang: scrap board out; screws picked; boxes clear of paper; paths open.
After scrape / before tape: dust wiped from joints; debris that would ride into mud gone.
After sand: vacuum preferred; no leaf-blower show; contain if other trades are adjacent.
After ACT: tile boxes out; wire offcuts; grid cutoffs; floor magnet for screws.
End of day vs end of stage: daily tidy keeps you fast; stage clean-out is what Job Check means.
Flip Cleaned Out only when true — then the office and GC can trust the board.

warnings.title: Lying to Monday
warnings.body: Marking Cleaned Out with scrap and mud buckets still on the floor teaches the board a lie the GC will remember.

variations.title: After sand
changes: No leaf-blower show next to other trades

quality_checks.prompt: Floor and paths clear for the next trade

common_mistakes.title: Daily tidy ≠ stage clean-out
common_mistakes.wrong: Flip chip after a quick sweep with piles left
common_mistakes.why: Office and GC trust the board
